paper: APPSC Group-II Services Preliminary (Screening) Test 2024 (Advt. No. 11/2023), held 25-02-2024 (Series A, GS/2G/200)

questions.s: 'Anda, harmika and chhatri' are integral parts of which one of the following Buddhist monuments ?
questions.x: A stupa is built of the anda (hemispherical dome), the harmika (railed platform on top) and the chhatri (umbrella).
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which among the following pillar inscriptions of Ashoka states that the land revenue rate of Lumbini was reduced to one-eighth ?
questions.x: The Rummindei (Lumbini) pillar records Ashoka's visit to the Buddha's birthplace and that the village was exempted from bali and paid only one-eighth (atthabhagiya) of the produce.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
a. Humayun brought famous painters Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad from Iran to Delhi.
b. Jahangir's reign is considered as the 'Golden period of the Mughal painting'.
c. During the reign of Jahangir, European painting was introduced at the Mughal court by the Danish merchants.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.x: Humayun did bring Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad, and Jahangir's reign was the high point of Mughal painting; European art reached the Mughal court through Portuguese Jesuits and the English, not Danish merchants, so only c is wrong.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which Mauryan officer was the incharge of Weights and Measures ?
questions.x: In the Arthashastra the Pautavadhyaksha superintended weights and measures; the Sulkadhyaksha collected tolls and the Panyadhyaksha oversaw trade.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Romaka Siddhanta written by Varahamihira deals with :
questions.x: Romaka Siddhanta is one of the five astronomical systems summarised by Varahamihira in his Pancha Siddhantika, so it deals with astronomy.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which one of the following books was not written by Harshavardhana ?
questions.x: Harsha wrote the plays Priyadarshika, Ratnavali and Nagananda; Kadambari is a prose romance by his court poet Banabhatta.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect with reference to Permanent Settlement ?
o: It was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in 1795.
It declared Zamindars as the owners of the land and they were given hereditary rights.
It was planned by John Shore.
The amount to be paid by the landlords was fixed.
questions.x: The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis in 1793, not 1795, so statement (1) is the incorrect one.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists :
List I (Delhi Sultans) - List II (Reforms)
a. Muhammad bin Tughlaq - I. Branding of Horses
b. Alauddin Khalji - II. Token Currency
c. Iltutmish - III. Development of Irrigation
d. Firuz Shah Tughlaq - IV. Introducing Silver Tankas
questions.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued token currency, Alauddin Khalji introduced branding of horses (dagh), Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka and Firuz Shah Tughlaq built canals for irrigation.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Among Ashtapradhans of Shivaji, the Sar-i-Naubat was associated with which of the following tasks ?
questions.x: The Sar-i-Naubat (Senapati) was the commander-in-chief of Shivaji's army.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists :
List I (Leaders) - List II (Revolt Centres)
a. Kunwar Singh - I. Kanpur
b. Hazrat Mahal - II. Delhi
c. Nana Saheb - III. Arrah, Bihar
d. Bakht Khan - IV. Lucknow
questions.x: In 1857 Kunwar Singh led at Arrah, Begum Hazrat Mahal at Lucknow, Nana Saheb at Kanpur and Bakht Khan commanded the rebels at Delhi.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was formed in Bombay in 1920. Who presided over its first session ?
questions.x: Lala Lajpat Rai was the first president of AITUC at its founding session in Bombay in October 1920.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which Act introduced the Communal Electorate System ?
questions.x: The Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Consider the following pairs regarding Carnatic wars :
Wars - Associated Treaty
I. First Carnatic War : Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
II. Second Carnatic War : Treaty of Yandabo
III. Third Carnatic War : Treaty of Paris
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched ?
questions.x: The First Carnatic War ended with Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) and the Third with the Treaty of Paris (1763); the Second ended with the Treaty of Pondicherry, while Yandabo (1826) closed the First Anglo-Burmese War.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: The Vaikom Satyagraha which started in Kerala was associated with :
questions.x: The Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25) fought for the right of lower castes to use the roads around the Vaikom temple and is a landmark of the temple entry movement.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: What was the code name of the Indian armed forces operation to liberate Goa, Daman and Diu from Portuguese rule ?
questions.x: The December 1961 operation that ended Portuguese rule in Goa, Daman and Diu was code-named Operation Vijay.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists :
List I (Governor-General) - List II (Treaty)
a. Warren Hastings - I. Treaty of Salbai
b. Lord Wellesley - II. Treaty of Bassein
c. Lord Minto-I - III. Treaty of Amritsar
d. Lord Hardinge-I - IV. Treaty of Lahore
questions.x: Salbai (1782) was under Warren Hastings, Bassein (1802) under Wellesley, Amritsar (1809) under Minto I and Lahore (1846) under Hardinge I.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which of the following is not a Harappan site ?
questions.x: Sohgaura (Gorakhpur district) is known for a Mauryan-era copper plate inscription, while the other three are Harappan sites.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which of the following inscriptions mentions the names of Vedic Gods Indra, Varuna, Mitra and Nasatyas ?
questions.x: The Boghazkoi (Anatolia) treaty of about 1380 BCE between the Hittites and Mitanni invokes Indra, Varuna, Mitra and the Nasatyas.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched ?
questions.x: The Battle of Chausa (1539) was fought between Humayun and Sher Shah, not by Jahangir.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological sequence :
I. Cripps Mission
II. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
III. Chauri Chaura Incident
IV. Poona Pact
questions.x: Chauri Chaura was in 1922, the Gandhi-Irwin Pact in 1931, the Poona Pact in 1932 and the Cripps Mission in 1942.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: By which one of the following Acts was the Governor-General of Bengal designated as the Governor-General of India ?
questions.x: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck was the first).
questions.subject: History

questions.s: During India's colonial period, the Downward Filtration Theory was related to :
questions.x: The Downward Filtration Theory held that educating the upper classes in English would let knowledge filter down to the masses; it was a colonial education policy.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Who said that "a single shelf of a good European Library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia" ?
questions.x: The line comes from Macaulay's Minute on Indian Education (1835).
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Which of the following is not correctly matched ?
Organisation - Person
o: Seva Samiti - Pandit Hriday Nath Kunzru
questions.x: Deva Samaj was founded in Lahore in 1887 by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri; Radhakant Deb led the orthodox Dharma Sabha.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Who among the following introduced the Blue Water Policy ?
questions.x: Francisco de Almeida, the first Portuguese viceroy in India, followed the Blue Water Policy of controlling the sea rather than building land power.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Lottery Committee (1817) of the British Rule was related to :
questions.x: The Lottery Committee set up in Calcutta in 1817 used lottery funds for town planning and civic improvements in the city.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Who founded the 'Indian Society of Oriental Art' to revive ancient art traditions of India ?
questions.x: The Indian Society of Oriental Art was founded in Calcutta in 1907 by Abanindranath Tagore (with Gaganendranath Tagore and others) to revive Indian art traditions.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Who among the following had resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council protesting Jallianwala Bagh Massacre ?
questions.x: Sir C. Sankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and martial law in Punjab.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched ?
o: Aligarh Movement - Sir Syed Ahmed Khan
questions.x: The Taiyuni movement was started by Maulana Karamat Ali Jaunpuri; Rashid Ahmed Gangohi was a co-founder of the Deoband school.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Lex Loci Act of 1850 ?
o: It prohibited child marriage below the age of 14.
It extended the prohibition of Sati all across British India.
It provided the right to inherit ancestral property to Hindu converts to Christianity.
It granted the legal recognition to widow marriages.
questions.x: The Caste Disabilities Removal Act (Lex Loci Act) 1850 protected the inheritance rights of people who changed religion, chiefly Hindu converts to Christianity.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. According to Continental Drift Theory, about 150 million years ago, Pangaea, the super continent, had split into Laurasia and Gondwanaland.
II. About 65 million years ago, Godwanaland further broke up to give rise to other continents.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: APPSC deleted this question in the final key.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Identify the incorrect statement :
o: At the focus of an earthquake, the energy is released.
The point on the surface nearest to the focus is called epicentre.
Epicentre is the first one to experience the waves.
Epicentre is a point directly below the focus.
questions.x: The epicentre lies on the surface directly above the focus (hypocentre), not below it.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Granite is a/an :
questions.x: Granite forms when magma cools slowly deep below the surface, which makes it an intrusive (plutonic) igneous rock with large crystals.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following :
List I (Landform) - List II (Geomorphic agent)
a. Delta - I. Waves and Currents
b. Cirque - II. Winds
c. Cliffs - III. Running water
d. Sand Dunes - IV. Glaciers
questions.x: Deltas are built by running water, cirques are carved by glaciers, sea cliffs are cut by waves and currents, and sand dunes are formed by wind.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: In which of the following layers of the atmosphere do meteorites burn up when they enter from the space ?
questions.x: Most meteors burn up in the mesosphere (about 50-80 km up), where the air is dense enough to cause friction heating.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following on heating and cooling of Atmosphere :
List I (Process) - List II (Mechanism)
a. Advection - I. Horizontal heating
b. Convection - II. Vertical heating
c. Insolation - III. Direct heating
d. Conduction - IV. Heating the lower layers
questions.x: Advection moves heat horizontally, convection moves it vertically, insolation is direct solar heating, and conduction from the ground heats the lowest layers of air.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. Kavaratti is the largest city in Lakshadweep Islands.
II. Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy Island of Lakshadweep from Maldives.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: Kavaratti is the administrative capital, not the largest settlement or island (Andrott is the largest island), and Minicoy is separated from the Maldives by the Eight Degree Channel, so neither statement is correct.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following :
List I (Ocean Bottom Relief) - List II (Characteristic feature)
a. Continental Shelf - I. Presence of canyons and trenches
b. Continental Slope - II. Associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes.
c. Deep Sea Plain - III. Presence of massive sedimentary deposits
d. Oceanic Deeps - IV. Presence of fine-grained sediments
questions.x: Continental shelves hold thick sediment deposits, the continental slope is cut by canyons and trenches, deep sea plains are covered with fine-grained sediments, and oceanic deeps are linked to active volcanoes and strong earthquakes.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Identify the correct arrangement of the following water bodies as per their salinity in decreasing order :
o: Lake Van > Dead Sea > Great Salt Lake
Dead Sea > Great Salt Lake > Lake Van
Great Salt Lake > Dead Sea > Lake Van
Dead Sea > Lake Van > Great Salt Lake
questions.x: Following the NCERT figures (Lake Van about 330 per thousand, Dead Sea about 238, Great Salt Lake about 220), the decreasing order is Lake Van, Dead Sea, Great Salt Lake.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which of the following mountains are young fold mountains ?
questions.x: The Alps were raised in the Alpine (Tertiary) orogeny and are young fold mountains; the Appalachians, Aravallis and Urals are old, worn-down fold mountains.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Prairies are the temperate grasslands present in :
questions.x: The Prairies are the temperate grasslands of the interior plains of the United States and Canada. APPSC's final key accepted both option (1) and option (3) for this question.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: The part of the Himalayas between Satluj and Kali rivers is called :
questions.x: Under the river-valley division of the Himalayas, the stretch between the Satluj and the Kali is the Kumaon Himalaya.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: The Eastern Ghats stretch from :
o: The Mahanadi valley to Seshachalam hills
The Mahanadi valley to the Nilgiris
questions.x: The Eastern Ghats run as a broken chain from the Mahanadi valley in Odisha south to the Nilgiris, where they meet the Western Ghats.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which of the following river forms the Dhuandhar waterfalls ?
questions.x: The Dhuandhar falls are formed by the Narmada at Bhedaghat near Jabalpur.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Pre-monsoon Mango Showers are common in the coastal areas of :
questions.x: Mango showers are pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and coastal Karnataka that help the mangoes ripen early; among the options only Karnataka fits.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: In India, very deep black soils are found in :
o: North-Western part of the Deccan Plateau
Eastern part of the Deccan Plateau
Southern part of the Deccan Plateau
South-Eastern part of the Deccan Plateau
questions.x: Black (regur) soils formed on the Deccan lava are deepest in the north-western Deccan (Maharashtra, Malwa and Gujarat).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: The most widespread forests in India are :
questions.x: Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests are the most widespread forest type in India.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following :
List I (River) - List II (Origin)
a. Vamsadhara - I. Nallamala hills
b. Machkund - II. Nandidurga hills
c. Gundlakamma - III. Jayapur hills
d. Pennar - IV. Mudugal hills
questions.x: The Vamsadhara rises in the Jeypore hills of Odisha, the Machkund in the Mudugal hills, the Gundlakamma in the Nallamala hills and the Pennar at Nandidurga in Karnataka.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Identify the incorrect statement :
o: The geographical extent of Laterite soils in Andhra Pradesh is very limited.
Laterites are formed in semi arid and low rainfall regions.
Laterites are less fertile and appear red and yellowish red.
Laterites can be used to grow Mango, Cashewnut orchards.
questions.x: Laterite soils form by intense leaching under high temperature and heavy rainfall, not in semi-arid low-rainfall regions.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following :
List I (Scheduled Tribe) - List II (State/Union Territory)
a. Gaddis - I. Sikkim
b. Jarawas - II. Jharkhand
c. Santhals - III. Andaman and Nicobar Islands
d. Bhutias - IV. Himachal Pradesh
questions.x: Gaddis live in Himachal Pradesh, Jarawas in the Andaman Islands, Santhals mainly in Jharkhand and Bhutias in Sikkim.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. The monsoons are primary winds.
II. The monsoons are confined only to the tropical lands lying between 20°N and 20°S.
III. Distribution of rainfall received from the South-West monsoons is governed mainly by the relief of the country.
Which of the above statements are correct ?
questions.x: APPSC deleted this question in the final key.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following :
List I (Functional classification of town) - List II (Example)
a. Mining town - I. Jamshedpur
b. Industrial town - II. Ankleshwar
c. Administrative town - III. Udhampur
d. Garrison Cantonment town - IV. Gandhinagar
questions.x: In the NCERT functional classification Ankleshwar is a mining (oil) town, Jamshedpur an industrial town, Gandhinagar an administrative town and Udhampur a garrison town.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which of the following oilseed crops is grown as 'rabi' crop only ?
questions.x: Rapeseed and mustard are sown in winter and grown only as rabi crops; groundnut, sunflower and sesame are also grown in kharif.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: In which region in India was tea plantation started in the first half of the 19th century ?
questions.x: Commercial tea planting began in the Brahmaputra valley of Assam in the 1830s-40s. APPSC's final key accepted both option (1) Brahmaputra valley and option (2) Darjeeling region.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following on industrial clusters developed by APIIC Ltd. in Andhra Pradesh :
List I (Location of the Industrial Cluster) - List II (Type of Industry)
a. Gandrajupalle in Chittoor region - I. Silk and Garments
b. Kopparthi in Kadapa region - II. Engineering
c. Makavarapalem at Visakhapatnam - III. Aluminium
d. Machilipatnam - IV. Jewellery
questions.x: APIIC developed a silk and garments cluster at Gandrajupalle, an engineering cluster at Kopparthi, an aluminium cluster at Makavarapalem and the imitation jewellery cluster at Machilipatnam.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: In which place in India was the first cement plant set up in 1904 ?
questions.x: India's first cement plant was set up at Madras (Chennai) in 1904 by South India Industries Ltd.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Which one of the following states is not connected with the Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) gas pipeline ?
questions.x: The HVJ pipeline runs from Hazira in Gujarat through Vijaipur in Madhya Pradesh to Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh; it does not pass through Maharashtra.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Bilaspur is the headquarters of which of the following Railway zones ?
questions.x: Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh) is the headquarters of the South East Central Railway; South Eastern is at Kolkata, East Coast at Bhubaneswar and East Central at Hajipur.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following on mineral resources of Andhra Pradesh :
List I (Mineral) - List II (Place in erstwhile districts)
a. Manganese - I. Forest areas of Visakhapatnam and East Godavari
b. Bauxite - II. Garividi in Vizianagaram
c. Mica - III. Jammalamadugu and Mydukuru in Kadapa region
d. Limestone - IV. Nellore Region
questions.x: Manganese is mined around Garividi in Vizianagaram, bauxite in the Agency forests of Visakhapatnam and East Godavari, mica in the Nellore belt and limestone around Jammalamadugu and Mydukuru in Kadapa.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following tourist spots of Andhra Pradesh :
List I (Beach) - List II (Nearest City / Town)
a. Suryalanka - I. Narasapuram
b. Manginapudi - II. Ongole
c. Kothapatnam - III. Machilipatnam
d. Perupalem - IV. Bapatla
questions.x: Suryalanka beach is near Bapatla, Manginapudi near Machilipatnam, Kothapatnam near Ongole and Perupalem near Narasapuram.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: To eradicate child marriages, a unique data driven approach like ALIVA is adopted by :
questions.x: ALIVA, a data-driven campaign to track adolescent girls and stop child marriage, was started by the Nayagarh district administration in Odisha.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: A circular structure used by Zoroastrians for excarnation or the disposal of human dead bodies through exposure to the natural elements and scavenger animals such as vultures is called :
questions.x: A dakhma (Tower of Silence) is the circular Zoroastrian structure where bodies are exposed to the elements and vultures.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: 'Diku Andi' means :
o: Marriage by exchange in Koya and Savara tribes
Marriage by capture in Naga tribes
Marriage by probation in Kuki tribe
Marriage by negotiation in Ho tribes
questions.x: Among the Ho tribe, Diku Andi refers to marriage arranged by negotiation, the form copied from non-tribal (diku) neighbours.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: The online portal developed by the Government of India for effective enforcement of the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, (which was amended in 2016), is :
questions.x: PENCIL (Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour) was launched by the Ministry of Labour in 2017 to enforce the child labour law.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. W.P. Scott defined divorce as 'an institutionalised arrangement for terminating the marriage relationship and allowing each partner the right to remarry'.
II. The first legislation in respect of the dissolution of marriage in India was enacted in 1869, and is 'Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act'.
III. The irresponsible departure from the home on the part of husband, leaving the family to fend for itself is called as 'the poor man's divorce'.
Which of the above given statements are correct ?
questions.x: Statements I and III are standard sociological definitions; II is wrong because the 1869 law was the Indian Divorce Act (for Christians), while the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act came in 1865/1936.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: Ravindra and Seema are husband and wife. Krishna and Madhavi are children of Ravindra-Seema. Madhavi is married to Harish and Jyothi is the daughter of Madhavi-Harish. Then the Consanguineous Kinship is between :
questions.x: Consanguineous kin are related by blood; Krishna is the maternal uncle of Jyothi, while the other pairs are related only through marriage (affinal kin).
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: As per the recommendations of the Sachar Committee, which among the following Muslim groups needs additional attention, similar to that of Hindu OBCs ?
questions.x: The Sachar Committee likened the Ajlaf (converts from occupational castes) to Hindu OBCs and the Arzal to Scheduled Castes; Ashrafs are the upper-status group.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: In the lines of Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013, which of the following Robots can be used to end India's manual scavenging ?
questions.x: Bandicoot, built by Kerala start-up Genrobotics, is a robotic manhole cleaner meant to replace manual scavenging; Vyommitra is ISRO's humanoid for Gaganyaan.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: In which of the following cases is it alleged that the verdict of the Supreme Court of India diluted the stringent provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 ?
o: K.C. Vasanth Kumar & Another vs State of Karnataka
Srish Kumar Choudhury vs State of Tripura
Om Prakash Mahajan vs State of Madhya Pradesh
Subhash Kashinath Mahajan vs State of Maharashtra
questions.x: In Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra (2018) the Supreme Court allowed anticipatory bail and preliminary inquiry under the SC/ST Act, which was widely seen as diluting it; Parliament reversed it by amendment in 2018.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: The Shuddhi Movement to bring back the people who transformed their religion to Islam and Christianity from Hinduism was started by :
questions.x: The Shuddhi (reconversion) movement was launched by Swami Dayananda Saraswati's Arya Samaj.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: India's first high-tech sports training centre for Divyangjan, 'The Atal Bihari Vajpayee Training Centre for Disability Sports' inaugurated on 2nd October, 2023 is located at :
questions.x: The Atal Bihari Vajpayee Training Centre for Disability Sports, India's first such centre, was inaugurated at Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: Under whose Chairmanship was a high-level committee on socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities of India set up by the Prime Minister's Office in 2013 ?
questions.x: The 2013 high-level committee on the status of tribal communities was chaired by Prof. Virginius Xaxa and reported in 2014.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: Who stated that 'I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved' ?
questions.x: The quote is from Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: After a landmark Judgement on Triple Talaq in 2017, which among the following methods of divorce practised in Muslim society was recently challenged in the Apex Court of India ?
questions.x: After Shayara Bano (2017) struck down instant triple talaq, petitions were filed in the Supreme Court in 2022 challenging Talaq-e-Hasan (pronounced once a month over three months).
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: Which among the following IT initiatives by the Ministry of Home Affairs facilitates dissemination of information about significant crimes, including Human Trafficking across the country on real time basis and enables Interstate co-ordination ?
o: Investigation Tracking System for Sexual Offences (ITSSO)
Special Police Unit for Women and Children (SPUWAC)
questions.x: The Crime Multi Agency Centre (Cri-MAC), run by the NCRB, shares alerts on significant crimes, including human trafficking, among police forces in real time.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: Who defined 'Communalism as the political assertiveness of a community to maintain its identity in a plural society undergoing modernization' ?
questions.x: This definition of communalism, as cited in Indian sociology texts, comes from Robert Melson and Howard Wolpe.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 enacted by the Government of India came into force from :
questions.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 received assent on 20 May 1961 and was brought into force from 1 July 1961.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. In the 15th Lok Sabha the percentage of elected women members in Lok Sabha had crossed 10% of its total strength for the first time.
II. The 17th Lok Sabha has a higher percentage of representation of elected women members than before and it is the highest ever since the independence of India.
III. The women members elected to the Legislative Assembly of Andhra Pradesh in General Elections 2019 was 11.74% of its total strength.
IV. The Women's Reservation Bill, 2023 got the assent of the President on 28th September, 2023.
Which among the above given statements are correct ?
questions.x: Women first crossed 10% of the Lok Sabha in 2009 (15th), the 17th Lok Sabha (about 14%) was the highest ever, and the Women's Reservation Act received assent on 28 September 2023; the AP figure in III is not correct (14 of 175 is 8%).
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: Under the pressure of groups interested in linguistic regionalism, the President of the Constituent Assembly of India has appointed the Linguistic Provinces Commission to report on creation of provinces of Andhra, Karnataka, Kerala and Maharashtra. In which year was this Commission appointed and who was it chaired by ?
questions.x: Rajendra Prasad, as President of the Constituent Assembly, appointed the Linguistic Provinces Commission under Justice S.K. Dhar in June 1948.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s:
Consider the following statements about the Assam Movement :
I. The Assam Movement led by All Assam Students' Union (AASU) was started in the year 1983.
II. The objective of the Assam Movement is to identify the migrant people, protect and provide constitutional, legislative and administrative safeguards to the Bangladeshi Migrants in Assam.
III. The Assam Movement was officially ended on 15th August, 1989 after coming to an understanding with the Government of India which found official expression in the Memorandum of Understanding popularly known as the Assam Accord.
Which of the above given statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: The AASU-led movement began in 1979, it aimed to detect and deport illegal migrants (safeguards were for the Assamese people, not the migrants), and it ended with the Assam Accord of 15 August 1985, so all three statements are wrong.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the PM CARES for Children Scheme :
I. The PM CARES for Children Scheme was launched by the Prime Minister of India on 11th March, 2020 for children who have lost their parents due to COVID-19 pandemic.
II. The PM CARES for Children Scheme inter-alia provides support to children through convergent approach, gap funding for ensuring education, health, monthly stipend from the age of 14 years and the child receives a lump sum amount of ₹ 10 lakhs on attaining the age of 18 years.
III. The children who have lost their legal guardian, adoptive parents or single adoptive parent due to COVID-19 pandemic are also entitled to benefits under the scheme.
Which of the above given statements are incorrect ?
questions.x: The scheme was announced on 29 May 2021, the stipend starts at 18 and the Rs 10 lakh lump sum is paid at 23, so I and II are wrong; III is correct because guardians and adoptive parents are covered.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: According to whom 'the existence of strong personal attachments and the fact of death, which of all human events is the most upsetting and disorganizing to man's calculations, are perhaps the main sources of religious belief' ?
questions.x: This functional view of religion as a response to death and emotional stress is Bronislaw Malinowski's.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: Which of the following Constitutional Amendments provided rights for making provisions in favour of the SCs and STs for relaxation of qualifying marks in any examination (or) lowering the standards of evaluation and for reservation in the matter of promotions to the public services of the Centre and the State ?
questions.x: The 82nd Amendment (2000) added a proviso to Article 335 allowing relaxation of qualifying marks and lower evaluation standards for SCs/STs in promotions.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: Identify the country with which the Union Cabinet of India has approved signing of Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for co-operation in disability sector that benefits the persons with disabilities (PwDs) ?
questions.x: In 2023 the Union Cabinet approved an MoU with South Africa for cooperation in the disability sector.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: A consensual and informal relationship practised in accordance to matrilineal laws of Kerala that prevailed among Namboothiris and Nairs is known as :
questions.x: Sambandham was the loose marital union between Nair women and Namboothiri (or Nair) men under Kerala's matrilineal marumakkathayam system.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: Recently the Delhi High Court has upheld the constitutional validity of a provision of the Hindu Marriage Act which 'prohibits marriage between people who are related to each other through ancestors from their parent's side unless their customs allow them to do so'. The said provision was mentioned in which Section of the Hindu Marriage Act ?
questions.x: Section 5(v) of the Hindu Marriage Act bars marriage between sapindas unless custom permits it; the Delhi High Court upheld it in January 2024.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: A Centrally sponsored scheme that aims to achieve the objectives of child protection, happy childhood and development under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is :
questions.x: Mission Vatsalya is the centrally sponsored child protection scheme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, aligned with the SDGs.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: Which of the following was the custom practised during the ancient period that allows married women to cohabit with a designated male for the sole purpose of procreating a child if her husband was impotent or had died ?
questions.x: Niyoga was the ancient practice allowing a woman to have a child by an appointed man when her husband was dead or unable to father children.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s:
As per Article 164(1) of the Constitution of India, a minister in charge of tribal welfare who may in addition be in charge of the Scheduled Castes and backward classes is compulsory for which of the following states ?
I. Madhya Pradesh
II. Punjab
III. Uttar Pradesh
IV. Jharkhand
V. Odisha
questions.x: The proviso to Article 164(1) requires a tribal welfare minister in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s: The comment 'Devotion cannot be subjected to gender discrimination' was made by the Apex Court in its judgement in the Sabarimala Case and permitted women of all age groups into the Sabarimala temple. Who among the following middle aged women first entered the Sabarimala temple after the Supreme Court judgement ?
questions.x: On 2 January 2019 Bindu Ammini and Kanaka Durga became the first women of menstruating age to enter Sabarimala after the 2018 verdict.
questions.subject: Indian Society

questions.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 9th Asian Winter Games :
I. The 9th Asian Winter Games 2025 are set to be held at Beijing, China.
II. The official slogan of the 9th Asian Winter Games 2025 is 'Dream of Winter, Love Among Asia'.
III. The names of the two tiger mascots of the 9th Asian Winter Games 2025 are Yingying and Nini.
IV. On January 11th, 2024 the emblem of the 9th Asian Winter Games 2025 'Breakthrough' was officially announced.
Which of the given above statements are correct ?
questions.x: The 2025 Asian Winter Games were held in Harbin, not Beijing, and the tiger mascots are Binbin and Nini; the slogan 'Dream of Winter, Love Among Asia' and the emblem announcement are correct.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: Which country was certified as Malaria-free by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2024 ?
questions.x: WHO certified Cabo Verde malaria-free on 12 January 2024.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Who among the following eminent personalities have been conferred with the Padma Shri Award 2024 for their contributions and achievements in the field of Arts ?
I. Drona Bhuyan
II. Ghulam Nabi Dar
III. Rajaram Jain
IV. Dasari Kondappa
V. Dukhu Majhi
questions.x: Drona Bhuyan, Ghulam Nabi Dar and Dasari Kondappa received the 2024 Padma Shri under Art; Rajaram Jain was honoured for literature and education and Dukhu Majhi for social work (environment).
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: According to INTERPOL, which State police had registered one of the first cases in India of human trafficking committed to force victims to commit cyber fraud ?
questions.x: INTERPOL cited a case registered by the Telangana police as one of the first in India of people being trafficked and forced to commit cyber fraud.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Match the following List I with List II with regard to Arjuna Awards 2023 :
List I (Name) - List II (Sports Discipline)
a. Ritu Negi - I. Golf
b. Sheetal Devi - II. Kabaddi
c. Naorem Roshibina Devi - III. Squash
d. Diksha Dagar - IV. Para-Archery
e. Harinder Pal Singh Sandhu - V. Wushu
questions.x: Ritu Negi plays kabaddi, Sheetal Devi para-archery, Roshibina Devi wushu, Diksha Dagar golf and Harinder Pal Singh Sandhu squash.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: Which among the following is the initiative by the Government of Karnataka in collaboration with the All India Game Developers Forum (AIGDF) with special emphasis on gaming and social media ?
questions.x: Karnataka launched the 'Digital Detox' initiative with the All India Game Developers Forum in 2024 to tackle excessive gaming and social media use.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: What is the theme of 'International Day of Education 2024' ?
o: Learning for people, planet, prosperity and peace
To invest in people, prioritize education
Education : A key driver for inclusion and empowerment
questions.x: UNESCO's theme for the International Day of Education on 24 January 2024 was 'Learning for lasting peace'.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. India's first National Highway steel slag road section is on NH-66 Mumbai-Goa National Highway.
II. Steel slag technology was developed by the Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) and Central Road Research Institute (CRRI).
III. JSW Steel, under the IGBC-CRRI technological guidance, has constructed a 1 km long four lane steel slag road section on NH-66 Mumbai-Goa National Highway.
Which of the above given statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: The first steel slag stretch of a National Highway is on NH-66 (Mumbai-Goa), but the technology was developed by CSIR-CRRI with the Ministry of Steel, not IGBC, so II and III are wrong.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: 'The Husavik Exploration Museum' seen in the news recently, belongs to which country ?
questions.x: Husavik is a town in northern Iceland; its Exploration Museum was in the news after giving an award to India.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Consider the following statements about MILAN 2024 :
I. MILAN 2024 is the 12th edition of Multilateral Naval Exercise being held from 19th to 27th February, 2024 under the aegis of Southern Naval Command.
II. The Harbour phase of MILAN 2024 is from 19th to 25th February, 2024 and is aimed towards building upon the experience of multilateral forces operating together at sea.
III. The Sea phase of MILAN 2024 is being conducted from 22nd to 27th February, 2024 and provides a platform for participating navies to discuss maritime subjects of common interest and share solutions.
Which among the above given statements are correct ?
questions.x: MILAN 2024 was hosted at Visakhapatnam by the Eastern Naval Command, the harbour phase ran 19-23 February with seminars and discussions and the sea phase ran 24-27 February with drills at sea, so all three statements are wrong.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: Which country has officially declared the 'Snow Leopard' as its national symbol, underscoring its commitment to conservation and ecological balance ?
questions.x: Kyrgyzstan declared the snow leopard its national symbol in January 2024.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
The Global Biofuel Alliance (GBA) was launched on 9th September, 2023 during the G20 Summit. Which among the following non-G20 countries are supporting the Global Biofuel Alliance (GBA) ?
I. Paraguay
II. Sri Lanka
III. Guyana
IV. Seychelles
V. Chile
VI. Finland
o: I, II, III, IV and V
II, III, IV, V and VI
I, III, IV, V and VI
I, II, III, IV and VI
questions.x: The non-G20 countries listed as GBA supporters at launch included Bangladesh, Singapore, Mauritius, UAE, Iceland, Kenya, Guyana, Paraguay, Seychelles, Sri Lanka, Uganda and Finland; Chile was not among them.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: The Government of Gujarat is set to launch the country's first Submarine tourism in collaboration with :
o: Daewoo Shipbuilding and Marine Engineering Co. Ltd
questions.x: Gujarat signed up with Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders for India's first submarine tourism project off Dwarka.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: A German-based company, Pepper Motion is set to invest ₹ 4,640 crores in its EV Bus and Truck manufacturing unit in 800 acres at :
questions.x: Pepper Motion's Rs 4,640 crore electric bus and truck plant was planned at Punganur in Chittoor district.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: In which state was the law guaranteeing 75% reservation for their local residents in the private sector struck down by the High Court stating the law is unconstitutional ?
questions.x: In November 2023 the Punjab and Haryana High Court struck down Haryana's law reserving 75% of private jobs for local residents.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. The Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) led by National Mission for Clean Ganga under the Ministry of Jal Shakti was launched at COP28 in New Delhi.
II. The Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) is a unique alliance covering 275+ global river cities in 11 countries.
III. The Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) is the first of its kind in the world.
Which of the above given statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: The GRCA was launched at COP28 in Dubai, not New Delhi, so I is wrong; it covers 275+ river cities in 11 countries and is described as the first alliance of its kind.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: Which among the following is incorrectly paired ?
o: Jagananna Chedodu : It provides a financial assistance of ₹ 10,000 per annum to Rajakas and Nayee Brahmins for better livelihood.
Jagananna Thodu : It facilitates a working capital loan up to ₹ 10,000 to the eligible poor, small and petty vendors with an intention to make them financially independent.
Jagananna Jeeva Kranthi Scheme : It aims to empower and provide social stability to women belonging to BC, SC and ST categories. The beneficiaries will receive sheep and goat units under this scheme.
YSR Navodayam Scheme : It aims to provide self-employment opportunities to the youth of Andhra Pradesh by creating job opportunities in the transport sector.
questions.x: YSR Navodayam was a one-time restructuring of MSME loans to relieve stressed micro, small and medium enterprises; it was not a transport-sector job scheme.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: The Centre of Excellence for Vegetables and Spices under the Indo-Israel Agriculture Project was proposed to be set up in :
questions.x: Under the Indo-Israel Agriculture Project, the Centre of Excellence for vegetables and spices in Andhra Pradesh was proposed in Palnadu district.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. Vijayawada Railway Station was awarded the 'Green Railway Station' certification with the highest rating of Platinum by Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED), USA.
II. Vijayawada Railway Station is the first in the South-Central Railway (SCR) Zone to have bagged the Platinum ring.
Which among the above given statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: Vijayawada station's Platinum green certification came from the Indian Green Building Council (IGBC), not LEED USA. The official key treats both statements as wrong.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Which among the following countries got membership into BRICS bloc with effect from 1st January, 2024 ?
I. Egypt
II. Argentina
III. Indonesia
IV. Ethiopia
V. Saudi Arabia
questions.x: BRICS invited Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Argentina to join from 1 January 2024; Argentina declined and Indonesia was not in this round, which leaves Egypt, Ethiopia and Saudi Arabia.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Identify the incorrect statement regarding 'PM Vishwakarma Yojana' Scheme :
I. The Government of India launched the 'PM Vishwakarma Yojana' Scheme to provide end-to-end support to fishermen with non-mechanized boats.
II. 'PM Vishwakarma Yojana' Scheme provides collateral free enterprise development loan up to ₹ 6 lakhs in two tranches.
questions.x: PM Vishwakarma supports artisans and craftspeople in 18 traditional trades, not fishermen, and its collateral-free loan is up to Rs 3 lakh (Rs 1 lakh plus Rs 2 lakh), so both statements are wrong.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. Dr. Tallavajhala Patanjali Sastri was conferred with Sahitya Akademi Award 2023 in Telugu Language for his poetry and poetry collections.
II. D.K. Chaduvula Babu was conferred with the Sahitya Akademi Bal Sahitya Puraskar 2023 in Telugu Language for his short stories 'Vajrala Vaana'.
III. Johny Takkedasila was conferred with the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar 2023 in Telugu Language for his book 'Devara Kotishu'.
Which of the above given statements are incorrect ?
questions.x: Patanjali Sastri won the 2023 Telugu Sahitya Akademi Award for a short story collection, not poetry, and statement III misstates Johny Takkedasila's Yuva Puraskar book; only II (Chaduvula Babu, 'Vajrala Vaana') is correct.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Identify the incorrect statements among the following :
I. Man Singh is the second Indian to win a gold medal at the Asian Marathon Championships.
II. Hardik Singh was named as Men's FIH Player of the Year at the International Hockey Federation Hockey Star Awards 2023.
III. Indian women's hockey captain Sushila Chanu won the FIH 'Best Goalkeeper of the Year Award' at the International Hockey Federation Hockey Star Awards 2023.
IV. Shubman Gill has been selected as 'Emerging Player of the Year' at International Cricket Council (ICC) Awards 2023.
questions.x: Man Singh's 2023 Asian Marathon gold and Hardik Singh's FIH Player of the Year award are correct; Sushila Chanu is not the captain or a goalkeeper (Savita Punia is the goalkeeper-captain), and the ICC Emerging Player of 2023 was Rachin Ravindra, not Shubman Gill.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: In which part of Andhra Pradesh is India's first largest private gold mine located ?
questions.x: India's first large private gold mine, the Jonnagiri project of Geomysore Services, is in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development for 2023 :
I. Daniel Barenboim was announced as winner of the Indira Gandhi Prize 2023 for his efforts to solve economic crisis and his contribution in the development of Sri Lanka.
II. Ali Abu Awwad was announced as winner of the Indira Gandhi Prize 2023 for his efforts towards a non-violent resolution of the Israel-Palestine conflict.
III. The International Jury of the Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development for 2023 was chaired by former Chief Justice of India, R.M. Lodha.
Which among the above given statements are incorrect ?
questions.x: Barenboim and Ali Abu Awwad shared the 2023 prize for work towards Israeli-Palestinian reconciliation (nothing to do with Sri Lanka), and the jury was chaired by former NSA Shivshankar Menon, not R.M. Lodha.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: Which among the following rare natural phenomenon is going to happen in 2024, after 221 years, in the United States of America ?
questions.x: In 2024 a 13-year and a 17-year periodical cicada brood emerged together in the US, a double emergence last seen in 1803, 221 years earlier.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Which among the following are incorrectly paired with regard to Swachh Survekshan Awards 2023 ?
I. Best SafaiMitra Suraksha Sheher : Prayagraj
II. Cleanest Ganga Town rank 2 : Varanasi
III. Cleanest Cantonment Board : Mhow Cantonment Board
IV. All India Cleanest City rank 3 : Navi Mumbai
questions.x: In Swachh Survekshan 2023 Chandigarh was the Best Safaimitra Surakshit Shehar and Varanasi ranked first (Prayagraj second) among Ganga towns; Mhow and Navi Mumbai's third place are correct.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Consider the following statements with regard to India Skills Report 2024 :
I. Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Kerala are the top three states with the highest availability of talent with computer skills.
II. Karnataka is the most preferred state to work for both male and female employable talent.
III. Telangana has the highest concentration of employable talent in the age group of 18 to 21 years.
IV. Andhra Pradesh is one among the states with the largest concentration of highly employable resources.
Which of the above given statements are correct ?
questions.x: The India Skills Report 2024 names Maharashtra, UP and Kerala for computer skills, Telangana for the 18-21 group and lists AP among states with the most highly employable talent; Kerala, not Karnataka, was the most preferred state to work in.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
Pick out the odd pairs with regard to newly elected Presidents of that respective country :
I. Fernando Pérez Molina : Guatemala
II. Abdel Fattah El-Sisi : Egypt
III. Felix Tshisekedi : Democratic Republic of the Congo
IV. Sierra Leone : Liberia
questions.x: Guatemala's newly elected president was Bernardo Arevalo (Otto Perez Molina was a former president), and Sierra Leone is a country, not Liberia's president (Joseph Boakai); El-Sisi and Tshisekedi were re-elected in December 2023.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s: Which is the first South Asian Nation to formally register same sex marriage ?
questions.x: Nepal registered its first same-sex marriage in November 2023, the first in South Asia.
questions.subject: Current Affairs
